questions.prompt: Who owns which truth in this app? Walk through the request flow and explain what the backend must enforce and what the frontend is allowed to own.

keyPoints.text: After register or login the server returns a JWT together with the user payload.
keyPoints.quote: Server returns JWT + user payload.

keyPoints.text: The client keeps the token in localStorage and Zustand, and Axios attaches it as a Bearer header.
keyPoints.quote: Client stores token in localStorage + Zustand.

keyPoints.text: Backend middleware validates the token on every protected route.
keyPoints.quote: Protected routes call API; backend middleware validates token.

keyPoints.text: Auth validation, workflow transition rules and query filtering/sorting/pagination are backend-owned.
keyPoints.quote: workflow transition rules

keyPoints.text: The frontend owns only UI state such as filters and modal visibility, plus pending loading/error states.
keyPoints.quote: current UI state (filters, modal open/close)

keyPoints.text: Transitions are validated server-side because the UI cannot be trusted alone.
keyPoints.quote: workflow transitions validated server-side (never trust UI only)

keyPoints.text: Every query is scoped to the authenticated user.
keyPoints.quote: all queries are user-scoped

questions.prompt: Explain how the backend is assembled at startup and why its pieces (entry point, DB bootstrap, validation, auth middleware) are arranged the way they are.

keyPoints.text: The entry point loads env, asserts JWT_SECRET, initializes the schema, registers middleware and mounts the domain routes.
keyPoints.quote: initialize DB schema

keyPoints.text: Order matters: the schema must exist before any handler runs.
keyPoints.quote: DB schema must exist before any route handler runs

keyPoints.text: JSON parsing must be registered before the POST/PUT handlers need a body.
keyPoints.quote: JSON parsing middleware must be active before POST/PUT handlers

keyPoints.text: Tables and indexes are created in code at startup so onboarding needs no migration step.
keyPoints.quote: no manual migration step for small project

keyPoints.text: Request contracts are centralized in one validation module so rules are not scattered.
keyPoints.quote: avoids validation logic being scattered across routes

keyPoints.text: One auth middleware gives every protected route the same gate and keeps handlers on business logic.
keyPoints.quote: all protected routes share one gate

questions.prompt: What correctness and security gaps does the deep dive document as verified against the source, and why does each one happen?

keyPoints.text: sort_by is interpolated into SQL and is safe only because the query schema restricts it to an enum.
keyPoints.quote: which is safe only because

keyPoints.text: A blank salary sent straight to the API becomes 0 because coercion runs before the empty-string branch.
keyPoints.quote: A blank salary sent to the API is stored as

keyPoints.text: Dates are validated by shape only, so an impossible date like February 30 is accepted.
keyPoints.quote: Dates are checked for shape only.

keyPoints.text: Duplicate registration is a check-then-insert race across an await, and the UNIQUE violation escapes the async handler.
keyPoints.quote: Two simultaneous sign-ups with the same email can both pass the check

keyPoints.text: Express 4 does not forward the rejected promise, so it becomes an unhandled rejection that ends the process.
keyPoints.quote: does not forward a rejected promise to the error handler

keyPoints.text: Login messages match, but skipping bcrypt for unknown emails leaks account existence through timing.
keyPoints.quote: Response time can therefore reveal which emails are registered.

keyPoints.text: The transition table is duplicated on the client with nothing keeping the copies in sync.
keyPoints.quote: They match today; nothing enforces that.
